textRun.content: 3825P / 7268P / 8568P: Cortech Barracuda Inmate Property Storage Box
Cortech Barracuda Box - Inmate Property Storage Box
Stack-and-Nest Polypropylene Property Storage Box in Three Sizes for Correctional Facilities
Cortech USA 3825P, 7268P, 8568P Barracuda Box - Inmate Property Storage Box
Headings marked [H2] should be set as H2 on the page.
Cortech Barracuda Inmate Property Storage Box

gives jails and prisons a tough, lightweight box for inmate property and records. Each box is molded in one piece from high impact “no break” polypropylene, with rounded corners and edges and vertical structural columns that help it stand up to impact.
The stack-and-nest design lets you stack boxes, with or without a lid, without crushing what is inside. Turn an empty box 180 degrees
and it nests inside another, which saves storage space and freight. There is a locking hasp on both sides of the box, and the matching Barracuda Box lid is sold separately.
One-piece injection-molded high impact “no break” polypropylene
Rounded corners and edges and vertical structural columns for strength and impact resistance
Stacks with or without a lid; empty boxes nest when turned 180 degrees
Locking hasp on both sides of the box
Flame retardant; passes California Technical Bulletin 133
Sold separately as the Cortech Barracuda Box Lid
Easy to clean, sanitize, and maintain
USA, made to ISO quality standards
The Barracuda Box is made for allowable in-cell storage and property rooms. With three sizes, facilities can choose the size that fits what each person is allowed to keep.
Inmate records and personal property storage

is a fully molded table for dining rooms, dayrooms, and activity rooms in correctional and behavioral healthcare facilities. The top and the x-shaped base are rotationally molded from high impact “no break” polyethylene, and the rounded edge of the top adds safety and comfort.

The legs attach to the top with tamper-resistant screws. The table can be bolted to the floor through concealed pilot holes with the Cortech Sabre Mount System, or the legs can be filled with sand to weigh it down. It comes in 42” and 48” round sizes with a plain top or a game top, and it is rated for outdoor use.

The seats attach to a continuous seam welded steel frame with tamper-resistant hardware through molded-in threaded steel inserts. Choose 1 to 4 seats, without arms, with arms at the ends, or with arms between every seat, and set the frame on tamper-resistant glides or bolt it to the floor.
One-piece rotationally molded high impact “no break” polyethylene with an antimicrobial compound
Molded-in threaded steel inserts give a tamper-resistant, steel-to-steel attachment to the frame
Continuous seam welded 2” diameter, 14-gauge powder coated steel with 11-gauge steel seat supports
No arms, arms at the ends, or arms between every seat
Optional table attachments, with variable table placement
Flame retardant; passes California Technical Bulletin 133
Easy to clean, sanitize, and maintain
Aqua, Black, Blue Gray, Brown, Burgundy, Canvas, Claylight, Gray, Green, Indigo, Midnight Blue, Moss, Overcast, Sand, Seagrass, Slate Blue, Stone Gray, or Tide (custom colors available on request)
USA, made to ISO quality standards
Frames come with tamper-resistant, nylon-bottom floor glides or a bolt-to-floor option
Each glide is anchored with a ¼”-16×3¾” anchor bolt, flat washer, and security Torx set screw (included), in a hole at least 2” deep; see Cortech instructions
The seats attach to the frame with tamper-resistant screws (T40 bit)
Structured Seating suits waiting areas and common rooms where seating has to stay in rows, stand up to heavy use, and be easy to clean.

Series section: Structured Seating is not part of the Cortech Endurance Series, so this page has no series section, only the About Cortech paragraph.

H1: I took out the dashes and "Rotationally Molded Design." Cortech does not publish model numbers for Structured Seating (the spec sheet says to contact Cortech for ordering information), so I kept your configuration numbers (10 to 45) under Available Models and Options and did not add them to the H1.

Variant name: "42 - 3 seats, with arms" should be "42 - 4 seats, with arms." Your page description and the variant weight (147 lbs, the same as the other 4-seat variants) both say 4 seats. Would you like it renamed?
Static load: your current page says 1,500 lb static load. The Cortech spec sheet says 2,000 lbs, so I used the spec sheet.
Testing: your current page says "Passes ASTM F1561-03." The Cortech spec sheet and web page do not say this, so I left it out.
Warranty: your current page does not list a warranty. The Cortech spec sheet says 3 years, but the Cortech web page says 5 years. I used the spec sheet. Which would you like?
Colors: your current page lists 7 colors and the Cortech web page lists 12. The Cortech spec sheet lists 18, so I used the spec sheet.
GREENGUARD Gold: this comes from the Cortech web page. The spec sheet does not mention it.
Layouts: your current page says the seating can be used in straight, U-shaped, or corner L arrangements. Cortech does not say this, so I left it out.
Dimensions: the Cortech spec drawing shows a 36” height and 19½” at the base. Cortech does not publish widths or weights. Your variants are set to 35, 62, 80, and 147 lbs, so I left them as they are.
Antimicrobial: the Cortech spec sheet says "Now infused with Cor-X antimicrobial compound," so I added "with an antimicrobial compound" to the Seats bullet.
Product images: the page has one image. Cortech has a photo of a 4-seat unit with arms between every seat. Would you like me to add it?

Cortech Endurance Cylinder Base Molded Table with Round Top

is a fully molded 42” round table for dining rooms, dayrooms, and activity rooms in correctional and behavioral healthcare facilities. The top and cylinder base are rotationally molded from high impact “no break” polyethylene, and the rounded edge of the top adds safety and comfort.

The base attaches to the top with tamper-resistant screws, and the table can be bolted to the floor through concealed pilot holes with the Cortech Sabre Mount System. An optional ballast door lets you add weight with sandbags. It comes with a plain top or a game top, pairs with the Cortech RazorBack Chair, and is rated for outdoor use.
Top and base rotationally molded from high impact “no break” polyethylene with an antimicrobial compound
Molded cylinder base; attaches to the top with tamper-resistant screws
Optional game top with a checkerboard pattern
Rated for outdoor use and UV stabilized
Tested to ISO 22196, showing a greater than 99% reduction in bacteria
Flame retardant; passes California Technical Bulletin 133 and UL 94 HB
Sound dampening, and easy to clean, sanitize, and maintain
Aqua, Black, Blue Gray, Brown, Burgundy, Canvas, Claylight, Gray, Green, Indigo, Midnight Blue, Moss, Overcast, Sand, Seagrass, Slate Blue, Stone Gray, or Tide (custom colors available on request)
USA, made to ISO quality standards

Optional ballast door for adding weight with sandbags (T27 bit); Cortech says not to use loose sand
The base attaches to the top with tamper-resistant screws and washers; see Cortech instructions

Series section: this is the same "About Cortech Endurance Series" section as on the EZ Bunk page.
H1: your current H1 lists only the 668S. I named the cylinder base, the same way as the X-base table pages, and added both model numbers.
Subtitle: your current subtitle says "Laminate Top," but this is the fully molded table. Cortech sells the laminate top version separately.
Model numbers: the Cortech spec sheet lists 668 (plain top) and 668GT (game top). Cortech photo names use 668S and 668GTS, the same as your variants, so I kept yours.
Variant names: your variants say "Solid Top." The Cortech spec sheet says "Plain Top," the same as on the Norix table pages. Would you like them renamed, for example "668S - Plain Top"?
Weight: both variants are set to 255 lbs. The Cortech spec sheet says 38 lbs (top 22 lbs, base 16 lbs), so I used 38 lbs for both.
Warranty: your current page says 10-year factory warranty. The Cortech spec sheet says lifetime warranty, so I used that.
Colors: your current page lists 12 colors. Cortech now lists 18, adding Canvas, Claylight, Moss, Overcast, Seagrass, and Tide. I used the Cortech list.
Ballast: your current page says the base can be filled with sand. Cortech now says to add weight with sandbags through an optional ballast door and not to use loose sand, so I used that.
Outdoor use: the FAQ on the Cortech product page says fully molded tables are rated for outdoor use and UV stabilized, so I added it to the description.
Product images: the page has five images. The last one is a color chart. Cortech now lists 18 colors. Does the chart show all 18?
